note: Objections a named critic actually raised, in their words, with a pointer to the moment. Mirrors questions/OBJECTIONS.md; that file is the reviewed artifact. Statuses: ANSWERED (a card has a prepared response), THIN (a card touches it but would not hold up as written), OPEN (nothing prepared; see the brief), N/A (not a question about the texts).

A.title: "Christ came for people, not animals."
A.text: Concede the priority, then show the texts never separate the two: Hosea 6:6 and its two uses by Jesus are about mercy as the thing God wants instead of sacrifice; Isaiah 11:6-9 and Genesis 1:29 frame the kingdom as the end of killing; Matthew 12:11-12 and Luke 13:15 argue from the animal to the person; the Clementine Homilies 3.45 put the displeasure with slaughter in Jesus's own mouth (held). The narrow claim: the gospel is for people, and its content includes how people treat what is in their power. Needs one paragraph on the sacrifice card with those five references checked in the held texts.

B.title: The monastic gradient
B.text: Dr. Pete's position: the church kept the abstinence for monks and fasts, which proves the tradition and also proves it was never meant for everyone. A good answer grants the history (the monastic diet is the preserved Nazarene practice, evidence for us), shows the gradient is Orthodoxy's later arrangement and not the first community's (Hegesippus on James, the Ebionites per Epiphanius, the Didache's Two Ways: no lay exemption), and says plainly what we ask of a layperson, the pastoral question the what-we-offer card handles for salvation and has not been asked for diet.

C.title: Virtue-signaling, grounding, and the culture of food
C.text: Not a source question. The answer is a way of speaking: never contempt for the table someone grew up at, the concession that the loudest advocates have often been the least grounded, and the plain fact that the people making this case have families. Needs two paragraphs on tone when diet comes up, written by someone who has had the conversation at a family dinner.

D.title: "The Theosophists invented it."
D.text: Answered 2026-10-10 on the sacrifice card, under "The Theosophical Society invented the vegetarian Jesus". The texts are held in christianity/Incoming/witnesses-on-flesh-and-sacrifice-selected-texts.md, with notes on what each does not say.

E.title: Theodicy of the many damned
E.text: The hell card needs one heading that joins the character argument to the texts: Luke 15 (the father runs), Matthew 18:14 ("not the will of your Father that one of these little ones should perish"), 1 Timothy 2:4 if we want to quote Paul against Paulinism, Thomas 113, and the plain reading of apollumi as destroy. "No loving parent would risk one child" is fine as a closer, not an opener.

objections.objection: Jesus kept Passover, so he ate the lamb.
objections.who: Dr. Pete (Orthodox, ER physician, author of The Athos Diet)

pointers.phrase: did Jesus eat lamb on Pasca

objections.heading: He kept Passover, so he ate the lamb
objections.answer: No gospel narrates him eating lamb; all three Synoptics narrate bread and wine at the central sacrificial meal. Kam's own reply on air: Jeremiah 7:22, the Syriac Luke 21:34 variant, and the Ebionite gospel's refusal of the Passover flesh (Panarion 30.22.4, which is Epiphanius quoting their alteration of Luke 22:15: evidence of what James's successors believed, not of what Jesus said).

objections.objection: The Temple cleansing targeted the money-changers' corruption, not sacrifice. The word is "thieves."

pointers.phrase: That word thieves seems to seems to lend

objections.heading: The Temple cleansing was about corrupt money-changers
objections.answer: Then explain why John specifies the sheep and the oxen, why Mark says he blocked anything carried through the court, and why he quoted Jeremiah 7, the chapter whose argument is that God never commanded burnt offerings. Kam's reply leaned on the Hebrew of Jeremiah 7:11 (parits, violent robber); keep that at reference level, we hold no lexicon.

objections.objection: Christ came to save mankind, not animals. Animal liberation is at best a side effect of the gospel.

pointers.phrase: he didn't come to the world to save animals

objections.answer: Nothing prepared. Kam conceded the priority and argued the anti-sacrifice stance follows from human salvation rather than competing with it; he cited the Orthodox canon forbidding clergy to hunt. The nearest card material (mercy outranks sacrifice) does not address the "not about animals" framing.

objections.objection: Is flesh forbidden for everyone, or a monastic calling? Orthodoxy keeps the abstinence for monks and fasts; is there a place for it for laypeople?

objections.answer: Nothing prepared. Kam answered with Eden and the Kingdom as the ideal and an ever-ascending state not everyone reaches. This is the strongest thing Dr. Pete said, because it grants the whole history and still keeps the steak.

objections.objection: Food is culture and family; questioning what people eat lands as contempt.

pointers.phrase: food is a very important aspect of our culture

objections.answer: Same as the previous one. Not an argument about the texts, an argument about how we speak.

objections.objection: There is no documented evidence Jesus was a vegetarian.

pointers.phrase: the idea that he was a vegetarian, there is no documented evidence

objections.heading: The people closest to him held the same line
objections.answer: Do not overclaim. James, not Jesus, is the attested vegetarian (Hegesippus, via Eusebius 2.23); the deep pass on the Nazarene claim says direct evidence about Jesus himself is thin and names the four holes. The claim we make is that the anti-sacrifice position is documented, inherited and central.

objections.objection: The Theosophical Society invented the vegetarian Jesus in the early 1900s.

pointers.phrase: the only writings that say he were came out of the Theosophical Society
Joshua was never linked with the Essenes

objections.heading: The Theosophical Society invented the vegetarian Jesus
objections.answer: Concede the modern texts (Ouseley's Gospel of the Holy Twelve, 1898-1901; Szekely). Then the dates: the Theosophical Society is 1875, and the witnesses are Romans 14:2 and 14:21 (c. 57), Hegesippus on James (c. 170), Clement on Matthew (c. 200), the Clementines, Eusebius on the disciples, Ancyra Canon 14 (314), all held; the vegetarian Bible Christian Church (1809); Bahrdt's Essene Jesus (1784-92). And concede where it bites: only Jerome (393) says the Essenes ate no meat, crediting Josephus, who doesn't.

objections.objection: There is no historical evidence for an Essene connection.

pointers.phrase: no historical evidence

objections.heading: Strongest Evidence
objections.answer: The sectarian vocabulary absent from the Hebrew Bible and present across the earliest Christian writings; the shared Isaiah 40:3 proof text; the organizational blueprint (twelve with an inner three, merged possessions, bread and wine, immersion); 4QMMT; the family succession through James.

objections.objection: Jesus and Paul do not contradict each other; the critics cherry-pick.

pointers.phrase: there's no contradictions between Jesus and Paul

objections.heading: Strongest Evidence
objections.answer: The letters almost never quote Jesus; James ruled and Paul reversed it in writing (Acts 15:19-20 against 1 Corinthians 10:25); James's letter answers the justification question the other way, naming the formula it denies.

objections.objection: Jesus could not teach the atonement before he died. Paul's teaching is the natural post-resurrection development.

pointers.phrase: why didn't Jesus even after his resurrection say that this is the pathway to be saved
because he hadn't died yet

objections.heading: The risen Jesus commissions commandments, forgiveness, and the kingdom
objections.answer: The post-resurrection silence is the answer. In the forty days the texts give him, he commissions the commandments, forgiveness delegated to people, repentance, and the kingdom, and never belief in a mechanism. Red text, held.

objections.objection: "Works of the law" means ritual observance, not good deeds, so Paul and Jesus agree.
objections.who: restated on the show; the scholarly form is Dunn and Wright

pointers.phrase: works of the law

objections.heading: 'Works of the law' doesn't mean good deeds
objections.answer: 4QMMT genuinely supports the reading and our own file says so. But it is a reading of Paul, not a source for Paul; it makes the break with Jerusalem sharper, not softer; and it doesn't reach Jesus's own words.

objections.objection: The Jerusalem church accepted Paul: the right hand of fellowship, Galatians 2:9.

pointers.phrase: right hand of fellowship

objections.heading: The Jerusalem church accepted him
objections.answer: Paul's own account of a meeting whose outcome he then overrode in practice; Acts 21:20-25 has Jerusalem still anxious about him a decade later.

objections.objection: Without Paul there is no gospel and no hope.
objections.who: Pauline pastors, restated on the show

pointers.phrase: Without Paul, we'd have no hope

objections.heading: Then what is Jesus to you? You've emptied him out.
objections.answer: The pastoral form of the Paul objection, and the room is won or lost here, not on Galatians. The whole card is the answer: the welcome is free and the life that follows is real; a mechanism is a smaller thing than what he is.

objections.objection: Everyone called him "Jesus" with a J in his own lifetime.

pointers.phrase: everyone called Yeshua Jesua with a J

objections.answer: Not ours to answer; a claim about Davis's own memory, not about the texts. The hosts noted the letter J postdates the period by a millennium. Nothing to prepare.

objections.heading: Hebrews 9:22; Leviticus 17:11
objections.answer: The hosts' reply (Jesus ate with sinners; if God cannot approach sin, sin has power over God) is on the card in sourced form: Mark 2:5 and Luke 7:48 forgive with no altar; Hosea 6:6 twice in Jesus's mouth; the Didache's prayers with no blood in them.

objections.objection: Tradition and the councils carry authority alongside, or above, the words of Jesus.
objections.who: Wes Huff, as restated on the show

pointers.phrase: Wes appealing to tradition instead of the words of Jesus

objections.heading: Who are you to sit in judgment over scripture?
objections.answer: Everyone reads with a criterion; ours is written down. Whatever Jesus said outranks what anyone said about him, and the Matthew 23:2-3 / Matthew 15 distinction (the seat affirmed, the superstructure contested) is his own.

objections.objection: God made a universe where most people are damned, and that is reasonable, because God is God.

pointers.phrase: I'm going to create this universe, billions of people, and only if they do this one specific thing

objections.answer: The hell card has the exegesis (Gehenna, destroy not torture, Thomas has no hell, the Jewish-Christian sources sort by deeds) but no theodicy heading. The hosts' reply, "no loving parent would risk one child," is an argument from character, not from text. The card needs a heading that joins the two.

objections.objection: Disliking a doctrine does not make it false. (Ehrman says he finds atonement distasteful.)

pointers.phrase: I find that distasteful and uh I don't I don't like the doctrine of atonement

objections.heading: Strongest Evidence
objections.answer: Lead with the texts, never with "I don't like it": Hosea 6:6, Matthew 9:13 and 12:7, the Didache 9-10 liturgy, and the incoherence argument in the research file, which argues incoherence, not taste.
